dialect.detail: Uses Micro Focus intrinsic routines CBL_CREATE_FILE, CBL_OPEN_FILE, CBL_CLOSE_FILE, CBL_COPY_FILE; also calls POSIX-style 'malloc', 'free', 'read', 'write' directly. Likely GnuCOBOL or Micro Focus compatible.

purpose.domain_detail: CTF (Capture The Flag) challenge program — filename is 'chall.cbl' and PROGRAM-ID is CBLCHALL1, implementing a menu-driven file manager with intentional security vulnerabilities (buffer management issues, fd manipulation).
purpose.summary: A menu-driven interactive program that allows creating, opening, reading, writing, closing, and copying files. It manages up to 16 file slots with malloc-allocated buffers and uses raw POSIX read/write calls alongside Micro Focus CBL_ file routines. The code contains deliberate security weaknesses (e.g., fd right-shift trick, unchecked buffer sizes) consistent with a CTF pwn challenge.

notable_features: CBL_CREATE_FILE / CBL_OPEN_FILE / CBL_CLOSE_FILE / CBL_COPY_FILE Micro Focus routines
Level-88 condition name used as loop terminator (ENDLOOP VALUE HIGH-VALUES)
DIVIDE 256 INTO ffd(fidx) GIVING tfd — intentional fd bit-shift trick
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
Fixed-format source with continuation lines using '-' in column 7
verdict.notes: The filename 'chall.cbl' and the deliberate security anti-patterns (heap buffer with unchecked size, fd manipulation via integer division) strongly suggest this is a CTF pwn/exploitation challenge. The dialect is ambiguous between GnuCOBOL and Micro Focus since both support CBL_ routines; GnuCOBOL is slightly more likely for a CTF context. No lines exceed 72 characters confirming fixed format.
